VISAKHAPATNAM: Cyclone Akvan over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by Tuesday evening and further strengthen into a very severe cyclonic storm around November 19 morning, the
India Meteorological Department (
IMD) said.
The storm is expected to continue moving northwestwards and cross the
Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni around noon on November 20 as a very severe cyclonic storm, with maximum sustained wind speeds of 120-130kmph, gusting to 145kmph.
Squally winds reaching 40-50kmph, with gusts up to 60kmph, began along and off the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts on Monday.
Wind speeds are likely to increase gradually as the system intensifies, with gale-force winds reaching 120-130kmph and gusting to 145kmph on November 19 and 20.
Sea conditions are likely to remain rough to very rough until November 17, after which they are expected to worsen, the IMD said.
According to the IMD, Akvan moved north-northwestwards slowly at a speed of 3kmph during the past six hours and remained centred over the central parts of the south and adjoining westcentral Bay of Bengal.
The cyclonic storm was located about 610km east of Chennai in Tamil Nadu, 630km northeast of Trincomalee in Sri Lanka, 660km southeast of Machilipatnam in Andhra Pradesh, 670km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh and 790km south of Gopalpur in Odisha.
The weather department said the system is very likely to continue moving north-northwestwards slowly and intensify further into a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by Tuesday evening.
Thereafter, it is likely to move northwestwards and intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm around the morning of November 19 before making landfall along the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts the following day.
Heavy to extremely heavy rainfall
The IMD has issued a red alert, warning of extremely heavy rainfall, for seven coastal districts, Kakinada, Konaseema, East Godavari, West Godavari, Eluru, Krishna and Bapatla, along with Yanam for November 19.
An orange alert has been issued for Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalle, Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore districts, warning of heavy to very heavy rainfall.
Srikakulam, Parvathipuram Manyam, Alluri Sitharama Raju (ASR), NTR, Palnadu and Tirupati districts are under a yellow alert for heavy rainfall on the same day.
For November 20, the weather agency has issued a red alert for Kakinada, Konaseema, East Godavari, West Godavari, Eluru, Krishna and Bapatla districts, along with Yanam.
An orange alert has been issued for Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, ASR, Anakapalle, NTR, Guntur, Palnadu, Prakasam and Nellore districts.
Srikakulam, Manyam and Tirupati districts are under a yellow alert for the day.
